content.content: 1 # Full spec (verbatim from user) — owner: supervisor — 2026-11-02 2 3 Constraints: Use only Node.js built-ins (no npm install). Node v22. Project's own tests must pass at the end. 4 5 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. 6 7 Server 8 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 9 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 16 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 17 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 18 19 API 20 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 22 - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 23 - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). content.text:
I graded the 10 new test files against the spec. The suite catches 13 of your 15 wrong implementations; items 9 and 14 are not caught, so it fails. I ran `npm test` and got 277/277 passing.

**Wrong-implementation check**

| # | Wrong implementation | Result | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Title trimmed with `trimEnd` | caught | `api-booking-rules.test.mjs:52` (`' X '` must be stored as `'X'`); also :51 and :55 |
| 2 | Same date+start kept in insertion order | caught | `api-routes.test.mjs:62-69` (Cosmos is created first, Aurora must come first); also :50-59 |
| 3 | 413 at >= 10000 bytes | caught | `api-booking.test.mjs:97-102` (exactly 10000 bytes must get 201) |
| 4 | 409 names the first-created overlap | caught | `api-booking-rules.test.mjs:144-149` (10:00 is created before 08:00, the message must say 08:00) |
| 5 | Date upper bound 2100 | caught | `api-booking-rules.test.mjs:64` (`2100-01-01` rejected), :67 (`2099-12-31` accepted); also `api-routes.test.mjs:111` |
| 6 | Memory changed before the save | caught | `persistence.test.mjs:93` (list empty after a failed POST), :99 (next id is still 1), :114 (booking survives a failed DELETE), :121 (id 5 not used up) |
| 7 | DELETE id accepting leading zeros | caught | `api-routes.test.mjs:167` (`'01'` with id 1 existing gives 404), :177 (booking still there) |
| 8 | Overlap check with `<=` | caught | `api-booking-rules.test.mjs:133-134` (back-to-back bookings before and after get 201) |
| 9 | Book re-enabled after the error is shown | **not caught** | The order is checked only on the 201 path (`page-behaviour.test.mjs:350`). The 409 test (:366-376), the fallback test (:378-385) and the no-reply tests (:387-407) only check the final `disabled === false`. |
| 10 | Filter value encoded | caught | `page-behaviour.test.mjs:216-221` (`'a b&c'` must be sent unchanged) |
| 11 | List refetched after a cancel with no reply | caught | `page-behaviour.test.mjs:460-467`, :452-458 (call count stays 3) |
| 12 | Stale list fetch error not ignored | caught | `page-behaviour.test.mjs:264-273` (stale error status), :275-283 (stale no-reply), :285-296 (stale success) |
| 13 | List text with a trailing space | caught | `page-behaviour.test.mjs:141` (exact `assert.equal`) |
| 14 | Content-type media type trimmed with `String.trim` | **not caught** | `api-booking.test.mjs:48-76` only has the space/tab accepted case (:73). Nothing checks that `\u00a0`, `\v`, `\f` or `\uFEFF` around `application/json` gives 415. |
| 15 | `?date=` treated as no filter | caught | `api-routes.test.mjs:110` (`?date` and `?date=` must get 400) |

**Code quality notes**
- **Duplication (the weakest area):**
  - `startServerOn3000` (`startup.test.mjs:130-146`) re-implements `spawnServer`/`buildEnv`, even though `startServer({ env: { PORT: undefined } })` already works.
  - `tmp`, `FIXTURE`/`FIXTURE_BOOKING` and `listeningLine` are copied between `startup.test.mjs` and `persistence.test.mjs`.
  - `assertError` exists in both `api-routes.test.mjs` and `booking-utils.mjs`.
- **Error handling:**
  - `persistence.test.mjs:164` calls `JSON.parse` inside a `'end'` handler, so a non-JSON reply throws outside the promise instead of failing the test cleanly. There is also no `res.on('error')` there.
  - `startup.test.mjs:143` resolves when the server exits, so a failed start only shows up later as a confusing stdout mismatch.
- **Weak assertions:**
  - `startup.test.mjs:160` only asserts when no `bookings.json` existed before.
  - `startup.test.mjs:284` compares file content only, so rewriting the same bytes at startup would pass.
- **Leftovers:** `pending` and `nextCall` in `fake-dom.mjs:140-141` are never used, and `nextCall` sets a flag inside its `find` callback.
- **Clean:** no `console.log`, no secrets, temp folders are removed through `t.after` or `finally`, and spec values are checked with exact equality.

## GRADE
Overall: 7/10
Verdict: fail
structure: 8 — helpers are focused and short; small mutation in a module-level `dateCounter`, the `find` callback in `nextCall` and a file-wide `unhandledRejection` listener
naming: 8 — clear and matches the code around it; `bad` (`startup.test.mjs:196`) is a poor name for a stringify helper, and `t` means both the test context and the boot result
duplication: 6 — a copied server launcher, plus `tmp`, fixtures, `listeningLine` and `assertError` repeated across files
size: 9 — every file is under 480 lines and every function under 50
errors: 7 — `sendChunked` can throw outside its promise and has no `res` error handler; the 3000 launcher hides a failed start; the JSON parse swallow in `request` is deliberate and fine
tests: 6 — strong boundary and order coverage, but wrong implementations 9 and 14 pass; a few assertions are conditional or weak
security: 10 — no secrets or unsafe input handling
leftovers: 8 — no console or debug code, but `pending` and `nextCall` are unused

- /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/test/api-booking.test.mjs:48 add rejected cases `'\u00a0application/json'`, `'application/json\u00a0'` and `'\uFEFFapplication/json'` (all 415), plus `'\vapplication/json'` and `'\fapplication/json'` sent over a raw `net` socket, because the Node http client refuses those characters
- /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/test/startup.test.mjs:130 delete `startServerOn3000` and use `startServer({ env: { PORT: value }, cwd })` from helpers
